caption: Antar v. Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa, LLC
citation_line: Antar v. Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa, LLC, No. 2:22-cv-05785, ECF No. 59 (D.N.J. Jan. 31, 2024), aff’d sub nom. Antar v. BetMGM, LLC, No. 24-1364 (3d Cir. Apr. 28, 2025)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Arleo dismissed Consumer Fraud Act and negligence claims brought by a self-described compulsive gambler who alleged that casino and online-gaming operators continued to entice him despite knowing of his addiction.
qualification_rationale: The ruling received national press attention and squarely addressed whether New Jersey’s detailed casino regime creates or leaves room for a civil duty to protect a known problem gambler who has not self-excluded.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit affirmed on April 28, 2025 in a nonprecedential opinion, agreeing that the complaint did not plausibly state CFA or negligence claims. The appellate disposition is persuasive but not binding precedent under the court’s internal procedures.
decision_selection_note: ECF 59 is a letter order granting the motions to dismiss and to compel arbitration, and the notice of appeal at ECF 60 is taken from it. No separate opinion accompanies it, so here the order is the decision. The caption conflict was an artifact of shortening: the full caption is Sam A. Antar v. The Borgata Hotel Casino and Spa, LLC; B Online Casino; BetMGM, LLC; MGM Resorts International, Inc.; Entain Plc, so Borgata is first-named and CourtListener indexes it under BetMGM.
